# Class 5 {.ct}

![](../graphics/REB_Logo.png){fig-alt="Reaction Engineering Basics Logo" fig-align="center" width="200"}

## Rate-Determining Steps and Quasi-Equilibrium {.cc}

Class 5 examines the generation of a mechanistic rate expression from a mechanism involving a rate-determining step. The concept and consequences of quasi-equilibrated mechanistic steps are explained.

## Learning Outcomes {.ch}

After completing Class 5 you should...

* Know
    * the definition of a rate-determining step
    * the defining equations for the apparent net rate of a non-elementary reaction in terms of the rate of the rate-determining step in its mechanism and quasi-equilibrium
* Understand
    * some mechanisms do not have a rate-determining step
    * when one step in a reaction mechanism is rate-determining, all other steps are quasi-equilibrated
* Be able to
    * generate a mechanistic rate expression from a mechanism that includes a rate-determining step
    * eliminate concentrations of reactive intermediates from mechanistic rate expressions using quasi-equilibrium expressions, when appropriate

## Prepare {.ch}

* Read Sections 4.4 and Example 4.8.2 from Chapter 4 of REB, The Book
* Watch the Class 5 Preparation Video
